summary: The chunk is comment-only, but the converter documentation omits delegated null and synchronization behavior, and two public comments retain unresolved NEEDS-HUMAN markers.

items.symbol: asJavaIterator and all newly documented JavaConverters conversion methods
items.issue: Every delegated conversion accepts a null source and returns null (`AsJavaConverters`/`AsScalaConverters` pattern-match on null), but each new comment promises a wrapper or view. `propertiesAsScalaMap` additionally says the result is always a new wrapper, which is false for null.
items.suggestion: State in every affected conversion's contract that a null argument produces null, and qualify wrapper/view claims to non-null arguments.

items.issue: The delegated `AsScalaConverters.asScala(java.util.Map)` contract requires callers to synchronize all non-atomic operations themselves when wrapping a synchronized Java map, including `get` when null values are possible. The new documentation omits this material concurrency limitation.
items.suggestion: Carry over the synchronized-map caveat from `AsScalaConverters.asScala(java.util.Map)` into this facade method's documentation.

items.issue: `Properties` can contain non-String keys or values, but `JPropertiesWrapper` blindly casts its entries to `String`; iteration and lookups can therefore throw `ClassCastException`. The new documentation presents it as an unconditional `Map[String, String]` view without this material limitation.
items.suggestion: Document that the wrapped properties' own entries must have String keys and values (or document the possible `ClassCastException`), in addition to the null result case.

items.issue: The added Scaladoc contains an unresolved `@note NEEDS-HUMAN` about whether this method's internal view may report non-empty when all `f` results are empty. The implementation confirms the stated discrepancy, but the intended public contract cannot be determined from the code.
items.suggestion: Have a maintainer decide whether to fix the `isEmpty` implementation or document its intended semantics; remove the NEEDS-HUMAN marker from the published Scaladoc.

items.issue: The added Scaladoc contains an unresolved `@note NEEDS-HUMAN` about this internal view's inverted `isEmpty` implementation. The code shows the discrepancy, but not the intended API meaning.
items.suggestion: Have a maintainer decide whether to correct `isEmpty` or document the intended behavior; remove the NEEDS-HUMAN marker from the published Scaladoc.
